spec: FINAL_SERVER_AUTHORITATIVE_EXECUTION_PLAN §11 (S11-infra-author)
Owner: infra-cofounder (author-only) + founder (apply). AUTHORED, NOT APPLIED.
THIS IS THE ONE DESIRED-STATE TRANSACTION FOR THIS BUCKET — do not apply the
bullets under §11 piecemeal; put-bucket-lifecycle-configuration replaces the
WHOLE document, so a second partial apply silently reverts this one.
LIVE POLICY CAPTURED VERBATIM 2026-08-15 (READ-ONLY, aws s3api
get-bucket-lifecycle-configuration --bucket shramsafal-uploads-prod) — THIS IS
THE ROLLBACK. It lives HERE, in this committed file (not only in a commit
message or a gitignored local capture/ folder), so it is durable in git
history. To roll back this whole change, re-apply exactly this document:
"Rules": [
"ID": "shramsafal-retention",
"Filter": {"Prefix": ""},
"Status": "Enabled",
"Transitions": [{"Days": 365, "StorageClass": "GLACIER"}],
"Expiration": {"Days": 2555}
(also re-saved verbatim by apply-config.sh into the capture/ subfolder it
creates on every run, timestamped — a second copy, not the only copy).
=== ROUND 1 REVIEW FINDING C2 — FIX APPLIED 2026-08-15 ===
§11 requires: 'Apply noncurrent rules ONLY to prefixes PROVEN to hold nothing
but reproducible artifacts.' Round 1 asserted '_deploy/, _deploys/, deploys/,
ai-sessions/ hold nothing but reproducible build/session artifacts' without
enumerating a single object key — an assertion, not the proof the section
demands, and the exact failure shape (measured on one thing, generalised to
another) this section's own 🛑🛑 header exists to prevent.
PROOF ATTEMPTED (read-only, 2026-08-15):
aws s3 ls s3://shramsafal-uploads-prod/_deploy/  --recursive --region ap-south-1
aws s3 ls s3://shramsafal-uploads-prod/_deploys/ --recursive --region ap-south-1
aws s3 ls s3://shramsafal-uploads-prod/deploys/  --recursive --region ap-south-1
_deploy/ (13 objects): mostly dotnet-publish tarballs named publish-<sha>.tar.gz
where <sha> is a real commit in this repo's history (verified: git cat-file -t
0d525d6e / 9929e897 / cdca7576 / f749d380 all return 'commit') — PLAUSIBLY
reproducible. But 8 of 13 objects are tagged with non-SHA short codes instead
(publish-diag/ff/rc/sv/swd/swd2/swd3/wav.tar.gz) with no way from the S3
listing alone to know which commit, if any, produced them — provenance
UNKNOWN. Plus api-binary-swap-2fd6eb99.sh, which does NOT appear in this
repo's git history (git log --all --diff-filter=A -- '*binary-swap*' finds
nothing); a same-named script exists only as an uncommitted local file under
_COFOUNDER/.local/ (a private, separately-governed tree this lane has no
standing to vouch for the durability of).
_deploys/ (15 objects): CONTRADICTS the reproducibility claim outright. 11 of
15 are one-off incident/deploy-runner scripts and SQL stamped with commit
5055d4b1 (a real commit — git cat-file -t 5055d4b1 -> commit) — but the
SCRIPTS THEMSELVES do not: purvesh-cleanup-COMMIT-5055d4b.sql,
prod-precount-5055d4b.sql, prod-precount-runner-5055d4b.sh,
recovery-runner-5055d4b.sh, r1-rollback-5055d4b.sh, schema-probe-5055d4b.sh,
user-probe-5055d4b.sh, env-probe-5055d4b.sh, step9-runner-5055d4b.sh,
cleanup-apply-runner-5055d4b.sh, migrations-apply-runner-5055d4b.sh — grepped
across the entire working tree and git history by exact filename fragment;
ZERO matches. These are hand/AI-authored incident-response artifacts from a
specific production event, existing ONLY in this S3 prefix. NOT reproducible.
deploys/ (1 object): agrisync-api-7f68ceb2.tar.gz — 7f68ceb2 is a real commit
(git cat-file -t 7f68ceb2 -> commit), matching project memory ('Trust Spine
7f68ceb2 DEPLOYED'). Same caveat as the SHA-tagged _deploy/ tarballs: a
rebuild-from-source claim, not independently verified byte-for-byte, and this
section's bar is 'proven', not 'plausible'.
VERDICT: the proof does NOT hold. Concrete non-reproducible content exists in
_deploys/, and provenance is genuinely unproven (not merely unlikely) for a
majority of _deploy/'s objects and the sole object in deploys/. Per this
review round's explicit instruction — 'If any listing shows non-reproducible
content, the rule does not ship' — the destructive action (Expiration +
NoncurrentVersionExpiration) is REMOVED from all three of these prefixes.
They now get NO lifecycle rule at all (same treatment as apk/) and inherit
only the bucket-wide AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload rule, which cannot touch
a completed object. This is MORE conservative than both the round-1 authored
state (a ~96-day destructive rule) AND the pre-existing live state (the
7-year bucket-wide rule these prefixes used to inherit) — the correct
direction to fail when proof is unavailable.
CONSEQUENCE, STATED PLAINLY: this leaves §11's original '618 MB of deploy
artifacts under a policy that doesn't fit them' cost problem UNRESOLVED for
_deploy/, _deploys/, deploys/. Fixing it properly needs one of: (a) a
write-time convention that tags genuinely-reproducible artifacts so a
lifecycle rule can target the tag rather than the whole prefix, (b) a
verified rebuild-and-diff proof per object class before authoring a deletion
rule, or (c) founder-directed manual pruning of the confirmed-non-reproducible
incident scripts in _deploys/. None of those is this lane's call to make
unilaterally — flagged as an open gap, not silently dropped.
ai-sessions/ is UNCHANGED in kind (still gets an expiry) but its number is
no longer borrowed from the RDS-snapshot-tied deploy horizon — see the next
block for why, and for its new, independently-reasoned value.
WHAT CHANGED AND WHY (now current, post-C2-fix):
1. Glacier transition REMOVED from the bucket, no replacement. Flexible
Retrieval cannot be read without a 3-5h restore or an expedited-retrieval
fee; one 'show me last season' tap would cost 13x-164x that photo's whole
annual storage bill. Nothing has transitioned yet (34/34 objects still
Standard as of the plan's own measurement; first transition would have
fired 2027-05-03) — this is a pure config replace, no restore/copy/cost.
Do NOT substitute Standard-IA (128 KB minimum billable size makes
thumbnails MORE expensive) or GLACIER_IR (deferred until attachments/
exceeds 100 GB — not close today).
2. The single bucket-wide rule is SPLIT BY PREFIX. The live rule carried
the farmer-evidence 7-year expiry AND the Glacier transition on the
SAME rule at prefix "" (bucket-wide) — so 'remove Glacier' is not a
separate edit, it means rewriting the rule that also carries the
farmer-evidence retention. Below, retention lives on attachments/ ONLY.
3. ai-sessions/ gets its OWN, independently-reasoned 7-day expiry — a fixed
constant, not computed. It used to borrow compute-deploy-horizon.sh's
RDS-snapshot-tied output, which was WRONG on reflection: that horizon
exists so a deploy artifact never expires before its paired pre-deploy
RDS snapshot might be used for rollback. ai-sessions/ holds AI
verification-poll image duplicates (per
docs/superpowers/evidence/2026-08-14-cost-data-footprint.md: 'useful
life is about sixty seconds'), unrelated to deploy/rollback pairing —
tying its expiry to RDS snapshot age was internally inconsistent bolted-
on reasoning left over from when it was grouped with the other three
prefixes. 7 days is a stated, reasoned safety margin (matches this
file's own AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload margin) over a ~60-second real
access pattern, for a prefix confirmed EMPTY today (0 objects, verified
live 2026-08-15) — so there is nothing this number could destroy yet.
NAMED PLAINLY (round-2 review non-blocking note): this is still an
UNPROVEN-CONTENTS prefix carrying a deletion rule — the C2 read-only-
listing proof that justified removing the rule from the other three
prefixes was never possible here (there is nothing to list). The
justification above is architectural/code-level reasoning about what
this prefix is FOR, not object-level proof of what it currently holds.
If ai-sessions/ ever holds something other than the AI-session image
duplicate this reasoning assumes, re-check before trusting this rule.
4. compute-deploy-horizon.sh is now UNUSED by this document (see its own
header) — kept in the repo for whenever _deploy/, _deploys/, deploys/
earn a properly-proven destructive rule.
apk/ GETS NO RULE AT ALL (by deliberate omission) — expiring it breaks live
APK download links. It still benefits from the bucket-wide
AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload rule below, which never touches complete
objects. _deploy/, _deploys/, deploys/ get the SAME treatment now, for the
reason above (C2), not because they are believed permanent — because their
reproducibility is unproven, and unproven means don't ship the deletion.
attachments/ keeps its 7-year Expiration (farmer evidence, unchanged in
substance) but LOSES the Glacier transition (item 1 above).
ai-sessions/ ALSO gets NoncurrentVersionExpiration at the same 7-day value —
this bucket has versioning ON (confirmed live), so a current-version
Expiration alone only inserts a delete marker and moves the bytes to
noncurrent; without a paired noncurrent rule the bytes never actually leave
the bucket. This pairing is NOT applied to attachments/ or apk/, is NOT
applied to _deploy/, _deploys/, deploys/ (per C2 above), and is NOT applied
anywhere on the raw bucket (see aws/raw/).
D9 CHECK (voice retention is FOREVER, per founder ruling D9): this bucket
does not hold raw voice audio — that lives in agrisync-raw-ap-south-1
(see aws/raw/lifecycle-policy.json, which authors NO expiration of any
kind). attachments/ here holds photos/receipts, not voice; its retention
is unchanged (still 2555 days) by this transaction. No rule in this
document shortens, transitions, or expires anything D9 covers.
AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload is bucket-wide and safe on every prefix —
it only cleans up multipart uploads that never completed; it cannot
delete or move a completed object.
